data.title: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Approves Five Energy Projects
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved five energy projects and facilities on Thursday in its effort to clear the way for critical natural gas infrastructure projects.

The approved projects include Sabine Pass's authority to operate three additional liquefaction trains at an existing terminal in Cameron Parish, La.

The commission has also issued Mountain Valley Pipeline a certificate to operate a project in Virginia and West Virginia to add 600,000 dekatherms per day of firm transportation capacity.

The approvals include a southeast Virginia energy storage project, a building certificate for the Forza Pipeline in New Mexico and Texas, and then an expansion of Texas Eastern's projects in Mississippi.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: States Move to Block Disney's Bid for Character.ai Assets — WSJ
data.description:
By Akiko Matsuda

A coalition of roughly 40 U.S. states filed an objection to bankrupt chatbot maker Character Technologies' proposed deal with Disney, arguing the transaction would benefit departing insiders and threaten consumer privacy.

The state attorneys general said in a Wednesday filing in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Del., that the deal is designed to "lock in" arrangements Disney made with Character before the bankruptcy filing and potentially transfer the private conversations of users of the Character.ai chatbot, including minors.

Under the proposed deal, Disney would pay $20 million for a nonexclusive license to use Character's intellectual property and artificial intelligence technology. The offer serves as a stalking horse bid, setting a floor price that can be topped by others at a court-supervised auction.

The bid excludes sensitive personal information such as raw user chat histories, but the states argued that what Disney plans to license — for example, AI models — is built on years of real consumer conversations and mental-health disclosures made by users while using the app. They asserted that the transaction should be scrutinized because many states prohibit the sale of that type of personal information.

A spokesperson for Disney didn't return a request for comment on Thursday.

In September, a month before Character filed for bankruptcy, Disney hired 66 of Character's 86 employees, including former Chief Executive Karandeep Anand, while obtaining legal releases protecting itself and those employees, the states said in the filing. The states said the prebankruptcy transaction is worth roughly $180 million in compensation and retention over three years.

The states said Disney retained the workforce, secured broad legal releases and dictated bidding procedures before the bankruptcy filing, so the transaction demands "heightened scrutiny."

Texas, in a separate filing, joined the coalition's objection, challenging that the transaction would block states from pursuing existing civil investigations into Character's practices.

The raw personal data collected by Character's chatbot platform has drawn a separate stalking horse bidder from an entity tied to Kai McPheeters, a co-founder of game developer Yonder. The states expressed concern over the proposed deal during a recent court hearing.

The states' pushback against Character's deal mirrors a wider fight over personal data privacy in corporate restructurings. Earlier this week, a New York judge approved Alphabet's acquisition of employee data from bankrupt Spirit Airlines after the Google parent company agreed to provide additional privacy protections.

Write to Akiko Matsuda at akiko.matsuda@wsj.com

data.title: TPG to take BILL Holdings private in $6 billion deal
data.description:
Fintech firm BILL Holdings said on Thursday it will be acquired by private equity group TPG, in partnership with Corpay , in an all-cash transaction valued at about $6 billion.

BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share. The offer represents a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average share price through November 16, the last full trading day before BILL takeover talks were reported.

The company was valued at a little under $5 billion before the media reports. Its shares fell about 3% in aftermarket trading.

Corpay is set to invest $1.10 billion in the fintech firm as part of the take-private deal, which would be accretive to Corpay cash EPS in 2027.

BILL provides cloud-based software that helps small and midsize businesses automate financial operations, including accounts payable and receivable.

Goldman Sachs and Qatalyst Partners were serving as financial advisors to BILL.

data.title: Foreign banks keep buying into India
data.description:
Fairfax Financial sold its whole stake in Indian lender IIFL Finance for about $370mn on November 18, raising cash for its $5.66bn takeover of state-controlled IDBI Bank.

The Canadian insurer's unit FIH Mauritius Investments offered more than 56mn shares at a floor price of INR611 ($6.54), 3.9% below the previous close, The Times of India reported. The block was worth about INR34.54bn, a person with direct knowledge of the trade told Reuters, and IIFL Finance shares climbed as much as 6.5% on the day.

Money is moving across Asia's borders into banks, and most of it is heading for India. In the same two days Japan's Daiwa Securities Group set out plans to grow in China and South Korea's Kakao Bank bought into a Mongolian lender. Both are spending profits earned in unusually strong home markets.

Foreign stakes in Indian lenders, deal value, $bn. Rupee values converted at November 18, 2026 ECB reference rates. Source: Government of India; Emirates NBD and RBL Bank; Reuters; The Indian Express. IntelliNews

A strike that did not stop the sale

New Delhi's Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on October 15 cleared the sale of 60.72% of IDBI Bank to a Canadian subsidiary of Fairfax Financial Holdings for INR528.78bn, or INR81 a share. The government is selling 30.48% and Life Insurance Corporation of India 30.24%, and officials expect the deal to be the biggest foreign direct investment yet in India's financial sector. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) must still judge the buyer fit and proper.

IDBI's staff unions want the deal scrapped. The United Forum of IDBI Officers & Employees held a two-day nationwide strike on November 2 and 3, calling the valuation inadequate and the process opaque, the Indo-Asian News Service reported. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) has argued that the sale breaches RBI rules limiting a foreign owner to 26% of the voting rights in an Indian bank.

The queue of foreign buyers

Fairfax would be the largest of several foreign buyers. Emirates NBD took 60% of RBL Bank on June 18 through a primary share issue worth about $2.75bn, which the two lenders described as the first purchase of a majority stake in a profitable Indian bank by a foreign bank, according to their joint statement. The Dubai bank's own Indian branches merge into RBL on December 1.

Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp paid INR134.83bn for 20% of Yes Bank, and Bank of America agreed in August to take up to 49.9% of Jio Credit, the lending arm of Jio Financial Services, for as much as INR182.68bn.

The books these buyers are paying for are much cleaner than a decade ago. Non-performing loans at Indian banks fell to 2.1% of gross loans in 2025 from 10% in 2017, according to World Bank data.

Indian banks' non-performing loans, % of gross loans. Source: World Bank (IMF Financial Soundness Indicators) via IntelliNews Lambda

Japan and Korea push outwards

Daiwa intends to expand cross-border M&A, listings and advisory work in China now that it owns all of its mainland securities venture, Nikkei Asia reported on November 18. Daiwa agreed in April to buy the 49% held by two Beijing state-owned partners for CNY706mn, Bloomberg reported at the time. 'We are the only Japanese brokerage with an investment banking license in China,' Zhu Hongxia, Daiwa's deputy head for Asia and Oceania, told the newspaper.

In Seongnam, south of Seoul, Kakao Bank on November 17 signed for 15% of M Bank, the digital lender of Mongolian conglomerate MCS Group, and became its second-largest shareholder. No price was disclosed. Mongolia is the Korean internet bank's third foreign market, after a stake in Indonesia's Superbank in 2023 and a holding in Thailand's planned virtual lender Bank X.

Paid for at home

Japan's three megabanks all raised their targets for the year to March 2027 on November 13. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group lifted its net profit goal to JPY2.8 trillion ($17.5bn) from JPY2.7 trillion and authorised a buyback of up to JPY200bn. Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group raised its forecast to JPY1.9 trillion ($11.9bn) from JPY1.7 trillion and added a JPY220bn repurchase. Mizuho Financial Group now expects JPY1.6 trillion, up from JPY1.4 trillion.

Each figure is above the record each group earned in the year to March 2026, when MUFG made JPY2.43 trillion, SMFG JPY1.58 trillion and Mizuho JPY1.25 trillion. Higher domestic interest rates have widened lending margins, and the groups are fighting over wealthy clients at home as well.

Japan's megabanks, net profit attributable to owners of parent, JPY trillion. Source: MUFG, SMFG and Mizuho results filings. IntelliNews

Those earnings, and the Gulf's, give lenders the capital to keep shopping abroad, and India remains the main destination. Whether the IDBI strike and the political objections can slow the flow will become clearer once the RBI rules on Fairfax.

This article was produced with the help of the IntelliNews Lambda analytical tool

data.title: Molson Coors Beverage Company Announces Regular Quarterly Dividend
data.description:
The Board of Directors of Molson Coors Beverage Company (, TAP.A) today declared a regular quarterly dividend on its Class A and Class B common stock of US$0.48 per share, payable December 18, 2026, to stockholders of record on December 4, 2026. The quarterly dividend is payable to holders of Class A and Class B common stock of Molson Coors Beverage Company.

In addition, the Board of Directors of Molson Coors Canada Inc. (TSX: TPX.B, TPX.A) today declared a quarterly dividend of approximately CAD$0.68 (the Canadian dollar equivalent of the dividend declared on Molson Coors Beverage Company stock), payable December 18, 2026, to its Class A and Class B exchangeable shareholders of record on December 4, 2026. The dividends declared in respect of the Class A and Class B exchangeable shares are eligible dividends for Canadian tax purposes.

OVERVIEW OF MOLSON COORS BEVERAGE COMPANY

For more than two centuries, we have brewed beverages that unite people to celebrate all life’s moments. From our core power brands, Coors Light, Miller Lite, Coors Banquet, Molson Canadian, Carling and Ožujsko to our above premium brands, including Madrí Excepcional, Staropramen, Blue Moon Belgian White and Leinenkugel’s Summer Shandy, to our value brands, like Miller High Life and Keystone Light, we produce many beloved and iconic beers. While our history is rooted in beer, we offer a modern portfolio that expands beyond the beer aisle as well, including flavored beverages like Vizzy Hard Seltzer and Monaco, spirits and non-alcoholic beverages. We also have partner brands, such as Simply Spiked, ZOA Energy, Fever-Tree, among others, through license, distribution, partnership and joint venture agreements. As a business, our ambition is to be the first choice for our people, our consumers and our customers, and our success depends on our ability to make our products available to meet a wide range of consumer segments and occasions.

To learn more about Molson Coors Beverage Company, visit molsoncoors.com.

ABOUT MOLSON COORS CANADA INC.

Molson Coors Canada Inc. ("MCCI") is a subsidiary of Molson Coors Beverage Company. MCCI Class A and Class B exchangeable shares offer substantially the same economic and voting rights as the respective classes of common shares of MCBC, as described in MCBC’s annual proxy statement and Form 10-K filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The trustee holder of the special Class A voting stock and the special Class B voting stock has the right to cast a number of votes equal to the number of then outstanding Class A exchangeable shares and Class B exchangeable shares, respectively.

data.title: Kincora Announces Shareholder Meeting Results
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Copper-gold explorer and hybrid project generator Kincora Copper Limited (Kincora or the Company) is pleased to announce the results of voting at its Annual General and Special Meeting ("AGM" or the "Meeting") on November 19th, 2026 at 4pm PST held by hybrid meeting with webcast from Vancouver, Canada.

All matters submitted to shareholders for approval as set out in the Company's Notice of Meeting and Information Circular, dated October 9th, 2026, were approved by the requisite majority of votes cast at the Meeting with 21.25% of shareholder proxies returned and very strong support for all matters of business.

Details of the resolutions are provided below. A copy of the presentation discussed at the Meeting will be made available on the Kincora website: https://www.kincoracopper.com/investors#services

Chairman Cameron McRae commented:

"At last year's AGM, we highlighted the importance of laying the foundations for Kincora's next phase of growth, with a share consolidation and strategic placement aligning key shareholders.

It is pleasing to reflect on how we have started to build on these and form a significant hybrid prospect generator providing unique portfolio exposure to large scale copper-gold discovery.

We are achieving a step change in scale with the drill bit, size of the project portfolio, management fee income and cash position. Today, Kincora is a more focused and better-capitalized company, with more metres going into the ground at more targets.

We are still in the early stage of execution with a very exciting 2027 ahead of us.

We thank our shareholders for their continued support and look forward to building on the progress achieved as we enter the next phase of Kincora's growth."

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION, PLEASE CONTACT:

  • Sam Spring, President and Chief Executive Officersam.spring@kincoracopper.com or +61431 329 345Executive office 400 - 837 West Hastings Street Vancouver, BC V6C 3N6, Canada Tel: 1.604.283.1722 
  • Kaitlin Taylor, Investor Relationsinvestors@kincoracopper.comSubsidiary office AustraliaC/- JM Corporate ServicesLevel 6, 350 Collins StreetMelbourne, VIC, Australia 3000

This announcement has been authorised for release by the Board of Kincora Copper Limited.

AGM details

Audited Annual Report

Shareholders received and considered the Financial Statements for the financial year ended December 31, 2025 and the report of the auditor thereon.

Number of Directors 99.72% For

Shareholders approved retaining the number of directors at five (5).

Election of Directors

Shareholders voted in favour of Kincora's management's nominees to the board of directors: Jonathan (Sam) Spring (99.69% For), John Holliday (99.71% For), Luke Murray (99.67% For), Cameron McRae (99.67% For) and James Durrant (99.69% For).

Auditor Appointed 99.80% For

Manning Elliot LLP was appointed Auditor of the Company to hold office until the next AGM or until its successor is duly appointed, and the directors were authorized to fix the Auditor's remuneration.

Approval of Issue of Placement Shares 99.48% For

Shareholders passed an ordinary resolution to ratify the issuance prior non-brokered private placement CDI's as described in the Information Circular.

Approval of Issuance Placement Options 99.52% For

Equity Incentive Plan (EIP) 98.29% For

Shareholders passed an ordinary resolution re-approving of amending the existing EIP as amended as described in the Information Circular.

Settlement of Debt 98.59% For

Disinterested shareholders passed an ordinary resolution for the settlement of debts as described in the Information Circular.

ABOUT KINCORA

Kincora Copper Limited is an emerging Australia-focused gold-copper explorer with a hybrid project generator strategy.

The Company is successfully proving up the prospectivity of its extensive project portfolio, which includes multiple district-scale landholdings and scalable drill ready targets. These assets are in Australia's Lachlan Fold Belt, one of the globe's leading porphyry belts, and the historical Condobolin mining field within the Cobar basin in NSW.

The Company has already unlocked over A$100 million of potential partner funding for multiple earlier stage and/or non-core porphyry projects. These initial deals have supported approximately 25,000 metres of drilling and over A$12m of partner funded exploration since late 2024, with management fees and exploration ramping up.

With a strong cash position of approximately A$13 million, and a further US$3.5-million due before year end (~A$5-million), the Company is now increasing sole funded exploration activities and increasing the scale of its project portfolio.

Various independent reviews have recently taken place supporting a formal process for the next leg of asset level partnerships for the remaining large scale porphyry projects.

During the Australian summer, Kincora plans to invest up to A$3 million in sole-funded, shallow air-core drilling advancing geological concepts and adding scale across four projects and 17 targets. Further to this, preparations are in place to undertake the first drilling in over twenty years at the outcropping mineralised Boree Creek project, which Kincora has a low-cost option over.

The programs are also expected to complement and enhance the value equation of asset-level partner discussions that are ongoing for the remaining 100% owned flagship and advanced exploration stage porphyry projects that are hosted in brownfield environments to existing world-class mines.

By having a significant portfolio of partner funded large porphyry projects and focused capital efficient programs at sole funded projects, the Company is seeking to position Kincora as a leading institutional grade explorer in the public Australian and Canadian markets, and the leading project generator on the ASX.

data.title: These were the only stocks that rose amid the stock market's wipeout Thursday
data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

All 11 sectors of the S&P 500 declined - 10 of them by more than 1% - but cybersecurity stocks bucked the weakness

Two cybersecurity stocks booked the biggest gains on Thursday, when only 38 of the S&P 500 were up for the trading sessions.

Only 38 stocks among the S&P 500 rose on Thursday amid a broad decline across the major U.S. indexes, as the successful completion of Anthropic's record initial public offering sucked the wind out of the market.

The stock market opened broadly higher, as strong demand for Anthropic's (ANT) IPO gave investors reason to be optimistic. But just as the artificial-intelligence giant's stock soared out of the gate, the market started sinking, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, the S&P 500 SPX and the Nasdaq Composite COMP all fell more than 2%.

At the top of the list of 38 stocks in the S&P 500 that rose on Thursday were Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Okta (OKTA), as worries about recent tech outages boosted demand for cybersecurity stocks. Both stocks were part of a screen published by MarketWatch early during the trading session.

data.title: LOT: Restarted production and first export position output for uranium-market upside

data.title: Revolution Medicines Presents Updated Phase 1/2 Data for RASONQUE® (daraxonrasib) Plus Chemotherapy in First-Line Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer at ENA 2026
data.description:
Key points:
  • With additional patients and longer follow-up, the combination of RASONQUE plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel demonstrated deep and durable responses in the first-line treatment setting
  • Results support the ongoing Phase 3 RASolute 303 trial in patients with treatment-naïve metastatic pancreatic cancer

REDWOOD CITY, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Revolution Medicines, Inc. , a global, commercial-stage oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers, today announced encouraging updated results from the Phase 1/2 RMC-GI-102 open-label study evaluating RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) in combination with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel (GnP) as a potential first-line treatment for patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The data will be presented today during a late-breaking oral session at the EORTC-NCI-AACR (ENA) Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics in Barcelona, Spain.

As of September 28, 2026, 61 patients in the first-line metastatic PDAC cohort of the Phase 1/2 RMC-GI-102 open-label study had received RASONQUE (200 mg) plus GnP, with median follow-up of 18.3 months. In the updated analysis, the confirmed objective response rate was 60.7% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 47.3–72.9), including complete responses in 8.2% of patients. The disease control rate was 90.2% (95% CI: 79.8–96.3) and median duration of response was 11.1 months (95% CI: 7.6- 18.4). Median progression free survival (PFS) was 12.8 months (95% CI: 10.8–18.4) and the twelve-month overall survival was 76.6% (95% CI: 63.7-85.4). The safety profile was consistent with the known safety profiles previously observed for both RASONQUE and GnP. This update builds on findings previously presented at the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) Annual Meeting in April 2026.

“With longer follow-up and a larger patient population, we are seeing a notable combination of high response rates, including deep complete responses, and durable disease control, with median progression-free survival exceeding one year,” said Wungki Park, M.D., M.S., medical oncologist at the David M. Rubenstein Center for Pancreatic Cancer Research at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, RMC-GI-102 and RASolute 303 investigator, and presenter of the data at ENA. “The emerging survival signal is meaningful and is estimated at 76.6% for patients to be alive at one year. Taken together, these findings provide a compelling rationale to further evaluate daraxonrasib as a potential first-line treatment option.”

“People with treatment-naïve metastatic pancreatic cancer urgently need more effective treatment options, given the limited clinical benefit of current chemotherapy regimens,” said Alan Sandler, M.D., chief development officer of Revolution Medicines. “The FDA’s recent Breakthrough Therapy Designation for RASONQUE plus GnP in this setting underscores the urgency of this work. The durability of treatment shown with these updated Phase 1/2 results is particularly encouraging and supports the ongoing Phase 3 RASolute 303 trial, which is evaluating RASONQUE both as a monotherapy and in combination with GnP versus GnP alone in patients with treatment-naïve metastatic PDAC, independent of tumor RAS genotype.”

The presentation (8LBA), titled “Daraxonrasib plus Gemcitabine/Nab-Paclitaxel (GnP) as First-Line (1L) Treatment for Patients (Pts) with Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (mPDAC),” will be delivered by Dr. Park during a late-breaking oral session on November 20, 2026, at the ENA Symposium in Barcelona, Spain.

About Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (PDAC)

Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, or PDAC, is the most common form of pancreatic cancer and among the most challenging malignancies. RAS, a key growth control switch in human cells, is the main driver of pancreatic cancer, which is characterized by excessive RAS signaling. Each year, approximately 500,000 people globally are diagnosed with PDAC and it is the seventh leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide.1,2

Because early-stage pancreatic cancer often causes few or no symptoms, approximately 80% of patients are diagnosed after the disease has spread, when treatment options are more limited.3 For patients with metastatic PDAC, the five-year relative survival rate is approximately 3% worldwide.4

About RASONQUE® (daraxonrasib)

RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) is an oral, RAS(ON) multi-selective, noncovalent, tri-complex inhibitor (TCI), approved by the U.S. FDA for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy.5 In the European Union, RASONQUE is approved by the European Commission for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy. RASONQUE is being investigated through a global Phase 3 registrational program in patients with PDAC and metastatic RAS mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Outside the U.S. and the European Union, RASONQUE is an investigational agent that has not been approved by any regulatory authority.

U.S. FDA APPROVED INDICATION

RASONQUE is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION FOR U.S. APPROVED INDICATION

RASONQUE is associated with the following Warnings and Precautions: Dermatologic and Soft Tissue Toxicity, Stomatitis and Oral Disorders, Diarrhea, Gastrointestinal Perforation, Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)/Pneumonitis, and Embryo-Fetal Toxicity.

WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS

Dermatologic and Soft Tissue Toxicity

RASONQUE can cause dermatologic toxicity, which may be severe. Clinical manifestations included, but were not limited to, rash, pruritus, paronychia, dry skin, and skin fissures. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, dermatologic toxicity occurred in 86% of patients treated with RASONQUE, of which 10% were Grade 3.

Monitor patients who develop dermatologic or soft tissue toxicities while receiving RASONQUE. Initiate prophylactic measures (e.g., topical corticosteroids, emollient creams, sunscreen, oral antibiotics) prior to the first dose of RASONQUE to reduce the risk of moderate to severe dermatologic reactions. Advise patients to limit sun exposure while taking RASONQUE. Initiate supportive measures (e.g., oral corticosteroids) as clinically indicated, and consider dermatologic consultation. Withhold, reduce the dose, or permanently discontinue RASONQUE based on severity.

Stomatitis and Oral Disorders

RASONQUE can cause stomatitis, including mouth ulcers and oral mucositis. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, stomatitis occurred in 57% of patients, of which 9% were Grade 3.

Monitor patients for signs and symptoms of stomatitis while receiving RASONQUE. Initiate a steroid-containing mouthwash for treatment of stomatitis and administer other topical treatments (e.g., chlorhexidine mouthwash, 2% lidocaine viscous) as clinically indicated. Withhold, reduce the dose, or permanently discontinue RASONQUE based on severity.

Diarrhea

RASONQUE can cause diarrhea. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, diarrhea occurred in 63% of patients, of which 6% were Grade 3.

If diarrhea occurs, administer antidiarrheal treatment as clinically indicated. Withhold, reduce the dose, or permanently discontinue RASONQUE based on severity.

Gastrointestinal Perforation

RASONQUE can cause gastrointestinal perforation. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, gastrointestinal perforation occurred in 0.9% of patients treated with RASONQUE, of which 0.5% were Grade 3, one event was Grade 4, and one event was fatal.

Monitor patients for gastrointestinal perforation. Withhold RASONQUE if gastrointestinal perforation is suspected. Reduce the dose or permanently discontinue RASONQUE if no other potential causes of gastrointestinal perforation are identified.

Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)/Pneumonitis

RASONQUE can cause interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ILD/pneumonitis occurred in 2.4% of patients treated with RASONQUE, of which 0.9% were Grade 3, and one event was fatal.

Monitor patients for new or worsening pulmonary symptoms. Withhold RASONQUE if ILD/pneumonitis is suspected. Reduce the dose or permanently discontinue RASONQUE if no other potential causes of ILD/pneumonitis are identified.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity

Based on findings in animals, RASONQUE can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with RASONQUE and for 1 week after the last dose. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with RASONQUE and for 1 week after the last dose.

ADVERSE REACTIONS

Serious adverse reactions occurred in 30% of patients treated with RASONQUE. Serious adverse reactions occurring in ≥ 2% of patients treated with RASONQUE were diarrhea (3.7%), pyrexia (3.3%), sepsis (2.9%), fatigue (2.1%), and hemorrhage (2.1%).

Adverse reactions leading to permanent discontinuation of RASONQUE occurred in 2.9% of patients, including two patients who discontinued due to rash (0.8%).

The most common (≥ 20%) adverse reactions in patients treated with RASONQUE were rash, diarrhea, stomatitis, nausea, fatigue, vomiting, abdominal pain, edema, decreased appetite, and hemorrhage.

DRUG INTERACTIONS

  • Strong CYP3A Inhibitors with P-gp Inhibition: Avoid concomitant use.
  • Strong CYP3A Inhibitors without P-gp Inhibition: Reduce RASONQUE dosage.
  • Moderate CYP3A Inhibitors with or without P-gp Inhibition: Reduce RASONQUE dosage.
  • P-gp Inhibitors: Reduce RASONQUE dosage.
  • Cyclosporine A: Avoid concomitant use.
  • Strong CYP3A Inducers: Avoid concomitant use. Increase RASONQUE dosage if concomitant use cannot be avoided.
  • Moderate CYP3A Inducers: Increase RASONQUE dosage.
  • P-gp Substrates: Take at least 4 hours apart from RASONQUE.

PROPHYLACTIC MEASURES

When initiating RASONQUE and throughout treatment, prophylactic and concomitant medications are recommended to reduce the risk of dermatologic reactions:

  • administer a topical corticosteroid (applied to the face and chest) and emollient creams;
  • advise patients to limit sun exposure and use broad-spectrum sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher); and
  • consider prophylactic oral antibiotics (e.g., doxycycline or minocycline).

Please see U.S. Full Prescribing Information for RASONQUE.

About Revolution Medicines, Inc.

Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-stage oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide. For more information, visit www.revmed.com and follow Revolution Medicines on LinkedIn, X (Twitter) and Instagram.

data.title: Revolution Medicines (RVMD) Reports 60.7% Response Rate in Phase 1/2 Study
data.description:
Key points:
  • With additional patients and longer follow-up, the combination of RASONQUE plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel demonstrated deep and durable responses in the first-line treatment setting
  • Results support the ongoing Phase 3 RASolute 303 trial in patients with treatment-naïve metastatic pancreatic cancer

In 61 patients with first-line metastatic pancreatic cancer, daraxonrasib plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel produced a confirmed 60.7% response rate and median progression-free survival of 12.8 months. The study was open-label, with 18.3 months’ median follow-up.

Material Details

#DetailAI Analyst View
1Confirmed response rate: 60.7% in 61 patientsThe response rate is a key efficacy signal, but comes from a small, open-label Phase 1/2 cohort.
2Median progression-free survival: 12.8 monthsThe reported disease-control duration supports further testing; no prior-period comparison was provided.
312-month overall survival: 76.6%This is an early survival signal from the study, not a controlled comparison.
4Median duration of response: 11.1 monthsResponse durability adds to the efficacy read-through, though the result remains from an early-phase study.
5Phase 3 RASolute 303 is ongoingThe Phase 3 trial will test whether the early-phase findings hold up against chemotherapy alone.

Context by AI Analyst

This is an updated early-phase clinical signal, building on findings presented in April 2026, rather than confirmatory evidence. The larger catalyst is the ongoing Phase 3 RASolute 303 trial, which will compare daraxonrasib regimens with GnP alone.
